newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: North to meet over blocked gold project.
newsitem.headline: North to meet over blocked gold project.

text.p: Mining and forestry group North Ltd said on Tuesday it will attempt to iron out environment concerns over its long-stalled Lake Cowal gold mine project during meetings with environmentalists starting on Wednesday.
However, the meetings represented little more than "another step along the way" in winning a go-ahead for the A$220 million project, a North spokesman said.

The New South Wales state Labor government in April 1996 refused a development application for the mine on environmental grounds linked to the discharge of cyanide after North had already spent some A$26 million on the project.

Wednesday's meeting will be attended by representatives from the Total Environment Centre and possibly other environment groups as well as the Australian Workers Union and the president of the New South Wales division of the Australian Labor Party, Peter Sams, the spokesman said.
Lake Cowal is one of the largest fresh water lakes in New South Wales.
Conservationists believe it is home to some 170 species of birds and needs to be protected.
North has projected the mine would produce 232,000 ounces of gold per year over the first seven years and 100,000 ounces per year over a remaining four-year mine life.
